title: Bahrain has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Qal'at al-Bahrain (2005), Pearling Path (2012), Dilmun Burial Mounds (2019)
summary: Qal'at al-Bahrain occupied since c. 2300 BCE, capital of Dilmun. Pearling site: 17 buildings in Muharraq, 3 oyster beds, Bu Maher Fort. Dilmun Burial Mounds: 21 sites, 2200–1750 BCE, 6 mound fields with over 10,000 mounds, 17 royal mounds. 6 tentative sites incl. Barbar Temple and Hawar Islands.

title: Hawar Islands — on UNESCO's tentative list for nature
summary: Islands about 26 km offshore, important for migratory waterbirds, coral reefs, seagrass meadows and a dugong (sea cow) population.

title: Barbar Temple — three temples built on top of each other
summary: Three temples built one over another between the 3rd and 2nd millennia BCE, with Sumerian-like architecture. On UNESCO's tentative list.

title: Bahrain startup ecosystem valued at $1.6bn, top-5 in MENA (GSER 2026)
summary: Value $1.6bn (Jul 2023–Dec 2025), +759% vs 2021 review. GSER 2026 (Startup Genome): MENA top 5 Performance, top 10 AI-Native, top 15 R&D.
